summary: The only material candidates in this window are a concentrated cluster of geopolitical shocks in its first half: an attempted military coup in Turkey followed by a three-month state of emergency and mass purges of police, army and judiciary, and a run of mass-casualty attacks in Western Europe (a vehicle/terror attack in France with over 80 dead, an axe attack near Wurzburg, a mall shooting in Munich). Nothing dated on or immediately before the flagged final day is of comparable macro significance, so if the model detected a regime change at the close of the window it more likely reflects the decay or aftermath of this earlier risk cluster than a fresh Day 14 catalyst.
mechanism: A failed coup and emergency rule in a large NATO-member economy, combined with repeated attacks in core European countries, raise geopolitical risk premia and safe-haven demand, widening the distribution of expected returns; the absence of further shocks in the second half of the window would equally allow that premium to unwind, which a price/volatility model could read as a state change.

claims.claim: Sections of the Turkish military attempted to seize power, described by the Prime Minister as an 'illegal attempt', with the President returning to Istanbul as the coup faltered.
Turkey's president declared a three-month state of emergency after the failed coup and ordered closure of thousands of private schools, charities and other institutions.

Around 8,000 police officers were sacked and more than 6,000 people in the army, judiciary and other state bodies detained; the US Secretary of State warned Turkey could lose NATO membership if democratic principles are not upheld.
France extended a state of emergency for three months following an attack that claimed over 80 lives, for which ISIL claimed responsibility.
Germany saw an axe attack on a train near Wurzburg and a shooting at a Munich shopping mall in which ten people including the gunman were killed.
By the second half of the window the Turkey story had shifted to mass rallies, including a cross-party 'Republic and Democracy' rally, rather than fresh escalation.

Items on the flagged final day concern monsoon flooding in Assam and Nepal, a jihadist group rebranding away from Al-Qaeda, North Korean rhetoric over US sanctions on its leader, and a US party nomination milestone.

US political developments through the window included both party conventions, the resignation of the Democratic National Committee chair after a leaked-email disclosure, and the nominee publicly calling on Russia to find missing emails.

competing_explanation: That the model flagged noise. The identified shocks are front-loaded in Days 1-9, while Days 10-14 contain only floods, regional violence, corporate deals (Verizon/Yahoo, Unilever/Dollar Shave Club, Tesla Gigafactory) and routine convention politics; North Korea's 'declaration of war' language over sanctions on its leader is rhetorical and unaccompanied by any described action. On that reading no item in the window plausibly triggers a change dated to the final day.
